utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could I remind you, Mr. Ismaili, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ismaili.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show the witness a document we had on the e-court yesterday. The name was a bit illegible, so I will ask the witness to put it on the ELMO so that he could tell us whether that is really his name. That was our document, 1D98, the page 1D1377.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, you had the same document on the screen yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still don't see it on our screen here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see now under the -- in the item 15, can you see and recognise your name and last name?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before your name, after the number 15, there is the number that OSCE used for the persons that he took statements from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now again to show the witness our number 1D98, but the page 1D1378 this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, sir, here, on the very top in the second line, there is again the same number that corresponded to your name on the previous page, and beneath it the statement that you gave to the OSCE is written. Does it remind you that on the 10th of January, 2002 you have indeed given a statement to the OSCE representatives when you complained to them also about the pains in your knees and legs?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you bring it closer so that I can see it better. Please can you zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is written in the English language and it contains, you see here, the quotation marks and there is your statement where it says what has happened to you. I will briefly summarize what you have stated in your statement to the Prosecutor that you were stopped at the check-point, that you were taken to the police station Butel, that you were ill treated there, and that you were taken to the Karpos police station later, that you were beaten with baseball bats by the reservists there, and that on Tuesdays at 2200 hours you were taken to court and all the other things that you already testified about in your statement to the Prosecutor. The only thing I'm asking you is whether this remind you now that you have given a statement to the OSCE on the 10th of January, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have given this declaration, but I'm not sure whether it was OSCE or The Hague, I'm not sure which one. I know that I gave this statement, yes. I was beaten up, I was maltreated and also I was taken to the Karpos police station, I was taken to the court. So everything which is written here is true. Because of --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, excuse me, but let me ask you this also. Do you remember, did you give a statement once only to some international representatives or was it that you gave a statement twice?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the declarations from 2001, from 2002 up to now. I have been looking after my own business. Then somebody came at home and they told me to go somewhere to give the statements. I told them what I experienced and then I came back to my family, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you complained also of the pains that you felt in your knees and your legs?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but I don't know who the people to whom I talked were, whether they were from The Hague or somebody else. This I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of this document it is written that you were complaining of pains in your knees and legs but also it is concluded that no bruises or any other injuries are visible.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the pains and all the scratches on the back of my body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you can confirm that the persons questioning you could not see on you any scars or some other injuries?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I have pain in the leg even today that I speak to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. We will now move to other issues that you testified about in your statement. You stated that on that Sunday around 9.00 heard shelling again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Around 1.00, you decided to leave the village, since you noticed that numerous families are leaving the village already; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere about 300 metres before the check-point at the location that you marked yesterday, you were stopped by the police, you were searched, and later you were let to continue your way to the check-point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the persons in camouflage uniforms, you could also see many civilians with various objects in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see civilians. I saw only people in uniforms, probably there were peasants with us. But we could not see who were there, exactly. It was, you know, full of noise and confusion there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say there was a lot of noise and confusion, could you agree with me if I say that more than a thousand people were walking from Ljuboten towards Skopje and that more than thousand people from the other side or from the neighbouring villages were also there in that area?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only civilians from Ljuboten. We went towards Shkup. There were no people from other villages; there were only peasants from Ljuboten there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were taken to court you described yesterday in detail also while answering my questions everything that took place there. Tell me, is it correct if I say that you don't know at all to what body is the police that is located in the court building attached; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Macedonian court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who were the superiors above the officers who are located, stationed in the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. We were actually kept in situations in which we could not see people who were around. Our head was down. We could not see where they had taken us. We didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't ask my question well. Once you were at the court, you stated that you have seen some police officers there in the court. So my question is: Is it correct that you have no idea who are the superior officers above those police officers in the court building. You don't know that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also testified about the events that took place when you were taken to the Sutka prison. You also don't know what are the bodies superior above the prison of Sutka, who should perform the controlled supervision over the prison. You don't know that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know either to which body are the prison guards in the Sutka prison attached and who is their superior body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Superior officer or body.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that it was Sutka prison, a prison of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were pardoned and released from remand prison, you never went to report what has happened to you and you never told your story about the events on the 12th of August to the police or to a judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not secure in order to lodge a complaint. We did not feel safe.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You could confirm before this Court that up to the present day neither you nor people you know are ready to respond to the summons from the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have received nothing, no request from the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally never received anything; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished witness Mamut Ismaili, my name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we represent Johan Tarculovski. I will ask you several questions related to the events between the 10th and the 12th of August, 2001. You have completed primary education in your native language, the Albanian, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until the 8th grade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 1989, you served a conscription military service in Novi Sad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1989, Novi Sad, yes, I did the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In which army branch were you serving? Could you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry. I was in infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you were trained in handling infantry weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the Sunday morning, you were at the Ljuboten village on the 12th of August, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On Sunday morning at 9.00, the shelling of the village started and you went into a cellar and you stayed there until 1.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is asking the counsel to do something about the headset because we have an echo and we can't hear the witness clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On Sunday morning at 9.00, the shelling of the village started and you took shelter in the -- in a basement, all the way until 1.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in my house with my family. I was there in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At 1.00, you joined the line walking towards Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: While you were walking within that line, the Macedonian security forces were shooting at the line moving towards Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were shots. We did not know where the shooting was coming from. We wanted to go to Shkup as soon as possible, that was our purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was your line shot at by the security forces and was someone hit?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not there where I was, no. We wanted to leave as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. After that you were taken to the Butel police station and from Butel police station you were taken to the police station Karpos; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the Karpos police station, you -- they gave you paraffin gloves. This is a test to a certain presence of powder particles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paraffin is not true. They took me to the room. My hands were up. I don't know what they did with my hands. My head was down and it wanted to pull me in one direction or another. I'm not sure whether it was paraffin or not. But this is indeed what I experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you they tell you that this is a test ascertain presence of particles of gunpowder on your hands?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me that question. They took me to the basement and they kept me there. They asked no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the Karpos police station, you were taken to the court where you gave a statement before an investigating judge in the presence of your attorney; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I had an attorney. I was in the room. Nobody was introduced as an attorney. I had no attorney there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown his statement, P52, page 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears, Mr. Apostolski, there's going to be a little delay until a technician finds what the problem is in displaying. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we use the same evidence -- the same exhibit, 1D100/1384. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I can see the signature, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. You've told the investigating judge that on that day that you were not a NLA member nor you are a member to another organisation, that that morning you were working in Radisani where you worked as a construction master and you were -- but then the judge did not trust your statement and you were assigned to go in remand prison, although you told him that you had two witnesses that you were in Radisani. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said a little time ago that you were in Ljuboten throughout the Sunday, all day Sunday on August 12th, and now you confirm that at 12.00 on Sunday you were in Radisani where you did some construction work. What is the truth, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is on Wednesday and Thursday, I worked in Radishan. There are some people there who were witness, there are three people who are witness who worked together with me. We worked in Radishan on Wednesday and Thursday. I don't know what they have said now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I just pointed out that on your statement you said that on the 12th of August, 2001 you have said that you've been Radisani and that you have two witnesses about it and I just pointed out to you that you previously said that you had been in the Ljuboten village. I'm just asking you now what is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I'm telling you the truth now, namely that Wednesday, Thursday, I worked in Radishan. Friday, I couldn't go there, neither did I on Saturday and Sunday. So only on Wednesday and Thursday, I worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Is it true that charges were filed against you in relation to the Ljuboten events on 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that the Skopje prosecutor's office filed charges against you in relation to the events in Ljuboten from 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. But I didn't do anything, nothing at all. It is true that they pressed charges against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that the president, Boris Trajkovski, pardoned you as a NLA member, and that's how the procedure against you ended?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. It was a pardon. We weren't in the NLA, I never was a member of the NLA. It was just a pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I forgot to propose at the end to have this 65 ter 1D100 to be tendered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, today you actually used 1D98. Yesterday you had 1D100. So that the document identified and probably the one that you should tender is 1D98.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I said that I didn't propose at the end of my questioning to have this record tendered into evidence. It is true that I used it with the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we have 1D98 and then 1D100 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the document that I showed to witness yesterday. It consists of two pages, so it's got 1D384 and 385; that is the Macedonian version. And the English version was 1D1386, 1D387.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second English page is 1D1387. And the Macedonian is 1D1385.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is the document you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have a few questions in relation to the statement that you gave in Skopje Court II in August 2001. Before you entered the room where the judge and the typist were sitting, were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before entering the court, we were beaten. They were -- we were asked to keep our hands behind our backs and they beat us greatly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And for how long did they beat you greatly?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly for how long. Maybe one hour it was. But to us it seemed like it was three or five hours, because of the great pains we suffered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how were the persons dressed who were beating you?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't look at them because our heads were down. We were not allowed to look up at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can go back for a second to the statement which was put to you by my learned colleague, 1D98. It says here: "We waited" --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The ERN of the page is N002-1109. If, please, the fifth paragraph could be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm reading it to you so that it gets translated, since it is in English. "We waited" -- "On Tuesday at 2200 hours, we were taken to courts. We waited three hours in one corridor where several reservists beat us. One policewoman stepped on our feet with her high heels." Is this an adequate description of what happened in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an adequate description of what happened in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're referring here to a policewoman. Why do you believe it was a policewoman?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was a female, that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why did you think she was in the police?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask her what she was and who she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But you said here in your statement she was from the police. But why do you think she was from the police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking for clarification. You said she was from the police. What did this woman wear to the best of your recollection today?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was dressed in uniform. That's why. But I didn't look at her carefully. Nobody allowed me to look up at her. I told you, we were keeping our heads low, but on -- I only saw that she was a female and she was cursing us all the time for no reason at all and beating us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same paragraph, because you were asked by my learned friend about being represented by a lawyer, it states that there was a private lawyer hired or contacted by your family but he arrived to court when all legal procedure had already finished; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My learned colleague also asked you about scars and bruises you suffered. On page 3, line 22 of the transcript, you said: "I had pains and scratches on the back of my body." How long were these scratches on your back visible?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were visible for four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you received them in the events in mid-August?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if we can please scroll in this statement to the very top, the statement which is in front of you, I'm referring to ID98 [sic]. So this statement is given by you on the 10th of January, 2002. At that time, they were no longer visible?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not have any scratches.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MAMUT ISMAILI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Ismaili, you will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber would like to thank you for your going to the lengths of coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give to us, and you are now able to return to your home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to thank you, Your Honour, for making it possible for me to come here. I wish you success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Am I correct in anticipating, Mr. Neuner, or Mr. Saxon, or Ms. Motoike, whichever, that the next witness has protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. And the witness will be lead by Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The issue is one of timing. It takes 20 minutes to prepare the technical equipment. I think what we should do to be most efficient in our use of time is to have the first break now, resuming at 3.35 and we will then have two almost hour and a half sessions to the end of the day. So we will adjourn now until 3.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now. Are you now receiving that in your language? Thank you. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Motoike has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I please have the usher's assistance in providing the witness with a document that bears ERN 0608-7695-0608-7695.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at this piece of paper. Without reading it aloud, could you tell us whether the information contained in that paper is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps after my learned colleagues have had a chance to look at this piece of paper and if they have no objections I would ask to tender it under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P224, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have been granted protective measures which means that you have face and voice distortion. That is, your face and your voice will be distorted for the public. You're also not being referred to not by your true name but by a pseudonym which is M-083 which we will refer to you as during the proceedings, or by "Witness". Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, to assist the Trial Chamber, because there are a number of documents I will be seeking to tender with this particular witness, we have made hard copies in a binder for today's proceedings. If we could have those distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, in 2001, were you an active police officer in the Macedonian police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. M-083.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, I am the counsel for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I move to the questions, from your data here I see that you speak and understand the language that I'm -- use, so I would like to kindly ask you when I ask the question, wait a while until the question is interpreted so that the Chamber and the colleagues in the courtroom could also follow what I'm asking and so that they could follow your answers. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You gave your personal data to my learned colleague the Prosecutor and I would only like to ask you whether it is correct that you were born and you live in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Skopje, you completed secondary school and after the conscription military service you were unemployed for two years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-083, that at that time in Macedonia the unemployment was a huge problem, and that the young people, once graduating from the school they would wait for many years until they find employment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that the duration of the wait for a job or the speed of finding a job was not related to the national affiliation of the individual but, rather, to the education that a person had and the need of the economy and other bodies for certain professional profiles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Are you asking about any religion and nationality in our state in relation to employment and education, or are you strictly highlighting some of them?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask whether there was any discrimination, as far as you know, with regards to the employment on the basis of national affiliation, or the length of waiting actually depended on the professional skills of the persons waiting for employment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Professional skills, as well as unemployment and demand for employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, one can also say that the situation exists even today in the Republic of Macedonia. Many people would go abroad to find a job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I do not know precisely, but mostly they do that also.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-083, previously in 2004 you gave a statement to the investigator of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of May of this year, when you arrived to The Hague, you then made certain addenda and corrections to the previously given statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Correction to my original first statement, is that what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Did you then give certain corrections and additions to a statement you have given previously.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Small additions and some change.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In those changes, when asked whether you gave a statement voluntarily, you stated that actually you were not giving it voluntarily but since you were summonsed, you believed that you needed to respond to the summons and then give a statement. Is that what you said to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I have responded to the summons as I should, as any normal citizen or as any member of our forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you were giving your statement, in your opinion, no force or coercion was used, just as a proper citizen you responded to the summons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But what you wanted to say is that before that summons that is sent threatening that you would you brought there by force if do not respond voluntarily, before that, nobody asked you whether you wanted voluntarily to talk to the investigators of the Prosecutor or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I understood it as a duty, as an obligation to respond to the summons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you now when you came to give a statement to the investigator, could you tell us, how long was the interview you then had with the ICTY investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Between 9.00 in the morning and 17, 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the interview with the investigator Thomas Kuehnel, you had an interpreter who interpreted the contents of your conversation with the investigator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that still what you were saying was not entered into the minutes immediately? Only at the end of that interview the minutes were composed, the minutes of that questioning, and then you signed the minutes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: The minutes were served at the end of the interview and then it was signed by me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You signed your statement in the English language, language you did not understand, but the contents of that text were translated to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And until the moment you arrived to The Hague, you were never given that written statement in your native language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Not until the arrival here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering that we changed the time for the break, I do not know whether an hour and a half has passed or could I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Another ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like to ask to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-083, that most of the duties that I have enumerated you were performing as a uniformed police officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Uniformed police officers in the Republic of Macedonia, pursuant to the law, were the authorised officials, and their rights, duties and responsibilities were based on the law; is that conclusion correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were working in the traffic police, you had also competences based on the Law on the Interior, Law on the Criminal Procedure, but also Law on the Safety of Traffic on Roads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order to maybe clarify those competences that you had, is it correct that based on the competences bestowed to you by the law as an authorised official you were able to stop any person that would violate the traffic ordinances, you could then issue a warning for that person, decide and impose, collect a fine immediately, or write a criminal report against that person? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes, and also detain persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding that part of the work when you find an offence, you did not need any special order because this was your authentic right and competence granted to you -- prescribed in the law for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you or your colleagues who worked with you, this time we took the example of the traffic police, if it would happen that the traffic accident had grave consequences so it would constitute a criminal offence, you would then inform the duty officer in the police station, that officer would inform the duty operational centre, 92, and the duty centre informed the investigating judge and the prosecutor. Is that the mode in which you operated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when, in the way that you have just indicated, the investigating judge would be informed, is it then correct that all further decisions about the procedure were made by the investigating judge and the police assisted. In actuality, it performed his or her orders and tasks given; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes, regarding grave criminal offences with the help of an investigating team in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-083, that the investigating judge would order that an investigating team is established and then with that investigating team, it would go on to the scene where the alleged crime took place and then an investigation would be performed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-083, that the investigating judge, when they are informed by the police, then they order that an investigation team is composed. They are including forensic specialists, doctors, et cetera, and then when they go to the scene, then everybody who is there act only upon the orders of the investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you also something else related to the performance and the responsibilities of the police. If I say that it is only the investigating judge the one who could interview someone, someone in a capacity of a witness, then, this statement of mine is correct, and in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Investigating judge can ask. His competences, I do not know to that extent, maybe he could do the interviewing with witnesses or without witnesses also.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the police could only gather some information from the citizens and it could never interview or interrogate the citizen as a witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: The police do receive information from citizens and then? Further in the sentence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe I was insufficiently clear. The police, pursuant to the Law on the Interior and the Law on the Criminal Procedure in the Republic of Macedonia, could just have an information hearing with persons to then compile an Official Note about it and then submit it to the prosecutor. My question is; is that correct; and is it correct --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- that you as police officers will no right to interrogate someone in the capacity of a witness. That was an authority belonging to the judge only; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes. Our task is to deal only with gathering of data and information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second break now and resume at 5.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-083, is it true that in the city of Skopje, the police stations that were within the city of Skopje were within the competences of the department of the interior of the municipality. For example, Centar, Cair, Kisela Voda, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While in the city of Skopje, which is a big city and is the capital of the republic, the department of the interior of these municipalities were within the sector of the interior of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Mr. M-083, that practically all police affairs, tasks and authorisations provided in the Law of the Interior and in the other laws were actually executed within the departments in the municipalities and the sectors for the interior in the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask to move into a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that PSOLO is also one of the police stations, and that is an acronym that in the Macedonian means a police station for securing persons and buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the police stations in the municipalities had their primary tasks to provide the security of the citizens of the public law and order, while the PSOLO was in charge to provide security to the persons and the securities, for example, the security of the president, the president of the government, ministers, diplomates that were in Skopje and also various buildings, such as the parliaments, the building of the government, the embassies, the post office, the television, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: It is true all but the post office and the television. They could only be secured by the municipalities where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware, Mr. M-083, that at the top, so to say, of the entire structure of the public security, so at the top of the professional line, both of the civilian and uniformed police was a director of the public security of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the director for public security was -- was appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, and is that correct, that also within the structure of the Ministry of the Interior was the state security headed by the director for state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also the director of the state security was also appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now something else, which is again linked to the execution of your duties as a police officer in the police stations and also on the other duties. Is it true if I were to say that you, in carrying out your duties pursuant to the law, also executed the duties based on the orders of your immediate superiors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "your immediate superiors," could that be understood as on the basis of the orders of the commander of your police station, his deputy, the head of the shift, the officer on duty, or the head of the department of -- for the interior? Would it be the circle of persons that would give orders to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your career you have never done it, and this is also not normal in the work of the police, you never received nor you were able to receive an order directly from the Ministry of Interior of the republic, so from that part of the ministry that is directly connected to the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Only my superiors in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand well: You only received orders from your superiors in the police station; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I could conclude from this that it would be absolutely wrong to say that as a police officer you could receive an order from the minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once you complete your duty, you and all the other police officers would write either Official Notes or reports and please tell me, is that correct that your reports about the execution of duties, you only submitted to your superiors in the police station; that is to say, in the department of the Cair municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can conclude from this that you never given oral or written reports to the Ministry of Interior or to the minister.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Never directly to the minister, only to the immediate superiors from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Answering the questions of my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, you spoke about the regular and the reserve forces of the police. Since the duties you mentioned carrying out probably do not give me the right to ask you about it in greater detail, so I will just ask few general questions to see whether some things could be made clearer. Is it correct that in normal circumstances outside of a crisis all the police duties are carried out by the regular police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Within the department of the interior, those duties are carried out by the uniformed police but also police working in civilian clothes, that is, more -- mainly the criminal police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All those police officers are regularly employed and receive a salary for their work; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that all citizens of a mature age, of an adult age, after serving the military service are deployed in some reserve duties so in -- so to be used in crisis situations or war; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a part of the people who have completed their military service are deployed in the reserve forces of the Macedonian army, another part is deployed in the reserve forces of the police, while some of them are in the civilian protection or in their company. Is that the way these things are organised according to the laws of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes. Unless for the civilian protection, I'm not really knowledgeable about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that all these duties and the way for the organisation of the reserve forces is also regulated by the laws of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you now: As a police officer at that time, do you know that in 1999, during the NATO campaign on Kosovo, a part of the reserve force was called, part of the police reservists were called to assist in securing of the safety of around 300.000 refugees that came to Macedonia from Kosovo? If you know that, can you answer; otherwise, if you have no personal knowledge about it, I will understand it as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: At that time (redacted), so I had no close contacts with the other police stations but the police duties as an active police officer. But it is possible. ?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since line 13 of page 60, the witness mentioned the time in which he was working on a certain position, which potentially might reveal his identity, I'd like to ask that the words (redacted) are redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. M-083, as a citizen of Macedonia, as a police officer, you probably know that in the spring of 2001 because of the terrorist attacks of the Albanian groups in the Republic of Macedonia there was a significant crisis situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes, there was a crisis situation at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that because of the terrorist attacks, the president of the country and the Security Council have ordered to call the reserve forces in the army and in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be true if I were to say that this situation with the terrorist attacks was actually a great surprise for all the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, exactly because of the fact that the Republic of Macedonia was the one to intensively help the Kosovo refugees and because of the fact that both in the government and in the parliament Albanian parties were represented as coalition partners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes. That part of the war looked a bit confusing in that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that although the police and the army were sending regular calls to the reserve forces to fulfil their duties, that people, because they were all taken by surprise and were afraid, they simply would leave the country and just a small number of people would respond to the calls to join the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Are you asking whether the Macedonian people were leaving the territory?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll make this question more simple. Do you know that only a small share -- a small percentage of the reserve forces reported to the calls in the first months; reports speak that the turnout was 5 to 10 percent. Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: According to the size of the incident at the beginning of the fights, the percentage was not very high, but it increased later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What you just answered, do you know that because of that initial small turnout, there was a public call for the people to report to the police and army units in order to defend its country from the terrorist attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: At the beginning of the fights, it became aware -- it became apparent that only the regular police forces could take care of the business, but then there was this call.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the position that you held, you know that people were called to join the reserve forces in your police station as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Probably within the department of the interior there was an official person who was in charge of the procedure -- of the procedure of calling and receiving the reserve forces and the volunteers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given the situation of crisis that became complicated mid-year, is it correct that the people that were called or who -- or those who reported upon their own initiative were frequently engaged in the municipalities without going through the entire procedure that was prescribed by the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: The reserve forces that were -- that had to go in the police stations but for the volunteers it was the superior officer who was -- who was obliged to check the past, or potential criminal past in order to admit them into the orders of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that check was not carried out in the police station but in the department of the interior in the municipality; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: The police stations were within the municipalities, so the superior officer who is in charge of these things is employed in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In respect to the reserve forces I would only ask you one more question, if you would be able to answer it. I'd like to ask you whether it's true that in that times of crisis it was difficult, it was very difficult to maintain full control over all the persons that have reported in the reserve forces of the police. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: You know, that is a mass of people, so I don't know what answer should I give to this question. It's not under my competence to know it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We would now go closer to the questions about which my learned colleague the Prosecutor asked you. I would like to ask you now to listen to what I'm about to say that will be a bit longer. If needed, I will repeat or I will break it into several questions, but I would like to know -- I'd like to know about the security situation in the territory of the Cair municipality. So basically if I were to say, Mr. M-083, that in the summer of 2001, the security situation on the Cair municipality territory was complicated because of at least the following reasons: One, the territory was occupied by an ethnically mixed population, about 80 per cent of them were ethnic Albanians; part of the municipality also encompassed the hills of Skopska Crna Gora which was an area that was of strategic importance for the city of Skopje; then because of the fact that above the village of Ljuboten, that is on the territory of Cair municipality there was the old road known as the Sultanov Put which connected the most endangered areas of Kumanovo with the Kosovo border. Then you could agree with me that these are only some of the elements that spoke about the difficult security situation in your municipality. Is it too complicated, or should I break this long question into shorter ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I will try to answer it. The old road connects Kumanovo part and the border towards Serbia, Tanusevci, so Skopska Crna Gora was really a problem of big importance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- is it correct that in the -- that you in the police station had reliable information that the village Ljuboten, located beneath that road, is used as a logistics base for the needs of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Although I was using the (redacted) (redacted), this question is not in my domain to answer. Only the special services could know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back a bit. I see that you told me that it was important that this road connected the border of Serbia through Skopska Crna Gora to Kosovo. I would like to ask you now: Did you mention also the border of Serbia? Because during that same time in southern Serbia there were terrorist attacks of various groups of the KLA, in the areas of Priseva [phoen], Podujevo, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: The old road above the village of Ljuboten is connected with the area known by the name of Ramno. I know if it is in direction it does connect all the points that have you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: May I interrupt for just a second. There is a reference to (redacted) in line 25 of page 64. If we could perhaps redact that, because I believe we're in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It doesn't appear to indicate the nature of the vehicle or ownership.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we go into private session so I can elaborate further?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which is what I should have said. Thank you for understanding me. And it will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-083, did you as a police officer in that environment have information that one part of the young people from the Ljuboten village joined NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did you in the police station have information speaking that part of the young people from Ljuboten, Albanians, joined NLA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-083
utterances.text: I personally did not have any information because my duty was (redacted). But the other colleagues from the station might have had.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He again mentioned his duty in line 22, so I would like to ask that -- that this (redacted) that is redacted from his answer and from my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to ask that we move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will need to adjourn now for the evening, and we resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. And we would plan to finish this witness and the next tomorrow, so I would ask all counsel to keep that in mind. We must ask you to return tomorrow morning at 9.00 to finish your evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 25th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
